use_when: Use type dialog to confirm an action before it happens, such as "Remove Luis Correia?", or for a short task that must finish before going back, such as an invite.
Use tone destructive when the action deletes or can't be undone; show what changes in the content rows, such as "Can be undone: No".
Use type sheet on mobile for filters, pickers and short choices that slide up from the bottom.
Ask a question in the title and name the thing, such as "Remove Luis Correia?", and put the result of the action on the main button, such as "Remove admin", not "OK".
Always give a way out: Cancel, the close ×, the Escape key and a click on the backdrop.
Place the dialog in the centre on a color/bg/overlay backdrop; place the sheet at the bottom, full width.

dont_use_when.when: For information people should read while they keep working: show it on the page, or in a toast.
For long forms or anything with more than one step: use a page with Stepper.
Open a modal from another modal.

variant_intent.dialog: confirm an action before it happens, such as "Remove Luis Correia?", or for a short task that must finish before going back, such as an invite
variant_intent.sheet: on mobile for filters, pickers and short choices that slide up from the bottom
variant_intent.destructive: when the action deletes or can't be undone; show what changes in the content rows, such as "Can be undone: No"

placement: Centred on a color/bg/overlay backdrop (the OnOverlay story); on screen, opened from a Button as a native modal dialog (the Open* stories).

a11y.fact: The root is a native <dialog>, so it has the dialog role; on screen it is opened with showModal(), which makes the rest of the page inert, keeps focus inside and returns it to the opener on close.
The dialog is named by its title (aria-labelledby) and described by its message (aria-describedby, only when a message exists).
Escape is cancelled and handed to onClose, so the owner decides when the dialog closes.
A click on the backdrop calls onClose; the dialog has no padding and the panel fills it, so only a press and release that both land on the backdrop count.
The close × is a native <button> with an accessible name (closeLabel, default "Close"); its icon is aria-hidden.
The sheet grab handle is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
The Content rows are a description list (<dl>, <dt>, <dd>), so each label stays paired with its value.
The actions are Horizon's ButtonGroup of native buttons; the first calls onAction, the second calls onClose.
